question: What should be the standard length of a tennis court according the laws of the International Tennis Federation (ITF), 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** According to the laws of the International Tennis Federation (ITF), 2021**, the standard length of a tennis court is **23.77 meters or 78 feet.**
 
• This measurement includes both the singles and doubles sidelines, which are **1.37 meters or 4.5 feet **away from the inner edge of the baseline.
 
• The width of the court is **8.23 meters or 27 feet **for singles matches, and **10.97 meters or 36 feet** for doubles matches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The International Tennis Federation (ITF) **is the governing body of world tennis, responsible for organizing and regulating international tennis tournaments and events, developing the sport globally, and setting and enforcing the rules of tennis.
 
• It was founded in **1913 and is based in London, England.**
 
• The** ITF is comprised of 210 member** associations, including national tennis federations and regional associations, and it is recognized by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** as the sole authority for tennis.
 
• The** ITF **works closely with other organizations such as the **Grand Slam tournaments, the ATP (Association of Tennis Professionals), and the WTA (Women's Tennis Association) to promote and develop the sport of tennis worldwide.**
